solution:
The normal vector is \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+2^2}=\sqrt{4+1+4}=\sqrt{9}=3\)
Unit normal: \(\hat{n}=\dfrac{\bar{n}}{|\bar{n}|}=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)\)
The distance of the plane from the origin is \(p=5\).
The normal form of the plane is \(\bar{r}\cdot\hat{n}=p\):
\(\bar{r}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)=5\)
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\right)=15\)
This is the required vector equation of the plane.

The given equation is \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+24\hat{k}\right)=13\), so \(\bar{n}=6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+24\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{6^2+8^2+24^2}=\sqrt{36+64+576}=\sqrt{676}=26\)
Divide both sides by \(|\bar{n}|=26\) to reduce to normal form \(\bar{r}\cdot\hat{n}=p\):
\(\bar{r}\cdot\dfrac{1}{26}\left(6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+24\hat{k}\right)=\dfrac{13}{26}=\dfrac{1}{2}\)
Hence \(p=\dfrac{1}{2}\).
\(\therefore\) the length of the perpendicular from the origin to the plane is \(\dfrac{1}{2}\) unit.

For \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+24\hat{k}\right)=13\), the normal is \(\bar{n}=6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+24\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{6^2+8^2+24^2}=\sqrt{36+64+576}=\sqrt{676}=26\)
The unit normal is
\(\hat{n}=\dfrac{1}{26}\left(6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+24\hat{k}\right)=\dfrac{3}{13}\hat{i}+\dfrac{4}{13}\hat{j}+\dfrac{12}{13}\hat{k}\)
The direction cosines of the normal are the components of \(\hat{n}\):
\(l=\dfrac{3}{13},\ m=\dfrac{4}{13},\ n=\dfrac{12}{13}\)
i.e. \(\left(\dfrac{3}{13},\ \dfrac{4}{13},\ \dfrac{12}{13}\right)\).

The plane passes through \(A(1,-2,1)\), \(B(2,-1,-3)\), \(C(0,1,5)\).
Two vectors in the plane:
\(\overline{AB}=B-A=(2-1)\hat{i}+(-1+2)\hat{j}+(-3-1)\hat{k}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-4\hat{k}\)
\(\overline{AC}=C-A=(0-1)\hat{i}+(1+2)\hat{j}+(5-1)\hat{k}=-\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
The normal is \(\bar{n}=\overline{AB}\times\overline{AC}\):
\(\bar{n}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\ 1&1&-4\\ -1&3&4\end{vmatrix}\)
\(=\hat{i}\big(1\cdot4-(-4)\cdot3\big)-\hat{j}\big(1\cdot4-(-4)\cdot(-1)\big)+\hat{k}\big(1\cdot3-1\cdot(-1)\big)\)
\(=\hat{i}(4+12)-\hat{j}(4-4)+\hat{k}(3+1)=16\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
Using \(A\) as position vector \(\bar{a}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\):
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(1)(16)+(-2)(0)+(1)(4)=20\)
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\) is
\(\bar{r}\cdot\left(16\hat{i}+4\hat{k}\right)=20\), i.e. dividing by \(4\),
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(4\hat{i}+\hat{k}\right)=5\).

The plane passes through \(A(1,-2,3)\) and its normal has direction ratios \((0,2,0)\).
The Cartesian equation of a plane through \((x_1,y_1,z_1)\) with normal \((a,b,c)\) is
\(a(x-x_1)+b(y-y_1)+c(z-z_1)=0\)
\(0(x-1)+2(y+2)+0(z-3)=0\)
\(2(y+2)=0\)
\(\therefore y+2=0,\ \text{i.e. } y=-2\)
This is the required Cartesian equation of the plane.

The required plane is parallel to \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(6\hat{i}+8\hat{j}+7\hat{k}\right)=0\), so it has the same normal direction \((6,8,7)\).
It passes through \(A(7,8,6)\). The Cartesian equation is
\(6(x-7)+8(y-8)+7(z-6)=0\)
\(6x-42+8y-64+7z-42=0\)
\(6x+8y+7z-148=0\)
\(\therefore 6x+8y+7z=148\)
This is the required Cartesian equation of the plane.

Let \(O\) be the origin and \(M(1,2,0)\) the foot of the perpendicular from \(O\) to the plane.
Then \(\overline{OM}\) is normal to the plane, so
\(\bar{n}=\overline{OM}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+0\hat{k}\)
The plane passes through \(M\) with position vector \(\bar{a}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}\).
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(1)(1)+(2)(2)+(0)(0)=5\)
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\) is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}\right)=5\)
This is the required vector equation of the plane.

The plane makes non-zero intercepts \(a,b,c\) on the coordinate axes, so its Cartesian (intercept) equation is
\(\dfrac{x}{a}+\dfrac{y}{b}+\dfrac{z}{c}=1\)
Multiplying throughout by \(abc\):
\(bc\,x+ca\,y+ab\,z=abc\)
Now let \(\bar{r}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}\). Then
\(bc\,x+ca\,y+ab\,z=\left(x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}\right)\cdot\left(bc\hat{i}+ca\hat{j}+ab\hat{k}\right)=\bar{r}\cdot\left(bc\hat{i}+ca\hat{j}+ab\hat{k}\right)\)
Hence
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(bc\hat{i}+ca\hat{j}+ab\hat{k}\right)=abc\)
which is the required vector equation of the plane.

The plane is parallel to \(\bar{b}=4\hat{i}+3\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}\), so its normal is \(\bar{n}=\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\).
\(\bar{n}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\ 4&0&3\\ 1&1&0\end{vmatrix}\)
\(=\hat{i}(0\cdot0-3\cdot1)-\hat{j}(4\cdot0-3\cdot1)+\hat{k}(4\cdot1-0\cdot1)\)
\(=-3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\)
The plane passes through \(A(-2,3,5)\), so \(\bar{a}=-2\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(-2)(-3)+(3)(3)+(5)(4)=6+9+20=35\)
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\) is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(-3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+4\hat{k}\right)=35\).

The plane is \(\bar{r}=\lambda\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\right)+\mu\left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\right)\).
Since there is no constant position-vector term, the plane passes through the origin, and it is parallel to \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
Normal \(\bar{n}=\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\):
\(\bar{n}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\ 1&1&-1\\ 1&2&3\end{vmatrix}\)
\(=\hat{i}(1\cdot3-(-1)\cdot2)-\hat{j}(1\cdot3-(-1)\cdot1)+\hat{k}(1\cdot2-1\cdot1)\)
\(=\hat{i}(3+2)-\hat{j}(3+1)+\hat{k}(2-1)=5\hat{i}-4\hat{j}+\hat{k}\)
The plane passes through the origin \((0,0,0)\), so the constant is \(0\).
Cartesian equation \(5x-4y+z=0\):
\(\therefore 5x-4y+z=0\).

A plane making equal intercepts \(a\) on all three axes has intercept equation
\(\dfrac{x}{a}+\dfrac{y}{a}+\dfrac{z}{a}=1\ \Rightarrow\ x+y+z=a\)
It passes through \(A(1,2,3)\): \(1+2+3=a\Rightarrow a=6\).
It passes through \(B(3,2,1)\): \(3+2+1=a\Rightarrow a=6\).
Both points give the same value \(a=6\), so the plane is
\(x+y+z=6\)
The vector equation is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)=6\).
(Note: with the equal-intercept condition \(x+y+z=a\), both given points force \(a=6\), so there is a unique such plane.)

A plane making equal non-zero intercepts \(a\) on the axes has
\(\dfrac{x}{a}+\dfrac{y}{a}+\dfrac{z}{a}=1\ \Rightarrow\ x+y+z=a\)
It passes through \((1,1,1)\):
\(1+1+1=a\Rightarrow a=3\)
Hence the Cartesian equation is \(x+y+z=3\).
The vector equation is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)=3\).

The line is \(\bar{r}=\left(\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)+\lambda\left(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)\), which passes through \(P(1,4,1)\) with direction \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
The required plane passes through the origin \(O\) and contains this line, so it contains the vectors
\(\overline{OP}=\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+\hat{k}\).
Normal \(\bar{n}=\overline{OP}\times\bar{b}\):
\(\bar{n}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\ 1&4&1\\ 1&2&1\end{vmatrix}\)
\(=\hat{i}(4\cdot1-1\cdot2)-\hat{j}(1\cdot1-1\cdot1)+\hat{k}(1\cdot2-4\cdot1)\)
\(=\hat{i}(4-2)-\hat{j}(1-1)+\hat{k}(2-4)=2\hat{i}+0\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\)
The plane passes through the origin, so its constant is \(0\).
\(\bar{r}\cdot\left(2\hat{i}-2\hat{k}\right)=0\), i.e. dividing by \(2\),
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}-\hat{k}\right)=0\).

The required plane bisects the segment \(AB\) at right angles, where \(A(2,3,6)\) and \(B(4,3,-2)\). It is the perpendicular bisector plane of \(AB\).
Midpoint \(M=\left(\dfrac{2+4}{2},\dfrac{3+3}{2},\dfrac{6-2}{2}\right)=(3,3,2)\).
Normal \(\bar{n}=\overline{AB}=(4-2)\hat{i}+(3-3)\hat{j}+(-2-6)\hat{k}=2\hat{i}+0\hat{j}-8\hat{k}\).
The plane passes through \(M\) with position vector \(\bar{a}=3\hat{i}+3\hat{j}+2\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(3)(2)+(3)(0)+(2)(-8)=6+0-16=-10\)
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\) is
\(\bar{r}\cdot\left(2\hat{i}-8\hat{k}\right)=-10\), i.e. dividing by \(2\),
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}-4\hat{k}\right)=-5\).

The normal vector is \(\bar{n}=2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{2^2+1^2+(-2)^2}=\sqrt{4+1+4}=\sqrt{9}=3\)
Unit normal: \(\hat{n}=\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\right)\).
The distance from the origin is \(p=42\).
Normal form \(\bar{r}\cdot\hat{n}=p\):
\(\bar{r}\cdot\dfrac{1}{3}\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\right)=42\)
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(2\hat{i}+\hat{j}-2\hat{k}\right)=126\)
This is the required vector equation of the plane.

The plane is \(6x-2y+3z-7=0\), with normal \((6,-2,3)\).
The perpendicular distance of the origin \((0,0,0)\) from \(ax+by+cz+d=0\) is
\(\dfrac{|a x_1+b y_1+c z_1+d|}{\sqrt{a^2+b^2+c^2}}\).
\(=\dfrac{|6(0)-2(0)+3(0)-7|}{\sqrt{6^2+(-2)^2+3^2}}=\dfrac{|-7|}{\sqrt{36+4+9}}=\dfrac{7}{\sqrt{49}}=\dfrac{7}{7}=1\)
\(\therefore\) the perpendicular distance of the origin from the plane is \(1\) unit.

The plane is \(2x+6y-3z=63\), with normal direction \((2,6,-3)\).
The foot of the perpendicular \(M\) from the origin lies along the normal, so
\(M=(2t,\ 6t,\ -3t)\) for some scalar \(t\).
Since \(M\) lies on the plane:
\(2(2t)+6(6t)-3(-3t)=63\)
\(4t+36t+9t=63\)
\(49t=63\Rightarrow t=\dfrac{63}{49}=\dfrac{9}{7}\)
Hence
\(M=\left(2\cdot\dfrac{9}{7},\ 6\cdot\dfrac{9}{7},\ -3\cdot\dfrac{9}{7}\right)=\left(\dfrac{18}{7},\ \dfrac{54}{7},\ -\dfrac{27}{7}\right)\)
\(\therefore\) the foot of the perpendicular is \(\left(\dfrac{18}{7},\ \dfrac{54}{7},\ -\dfrac{27}{7}\right)\).

The given plane is \(\bar{r}\cdot\left(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+12\hat{k}\right)=78\), so \(\bar{n}=3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+12\hat{k}\).
\(|\bar{n}|=\sqrt{3^2+4^2+12^2}=\sqrt{9+16+144}=\sqrt{169}=13\)
Divide both sides by \(13\) to obtain the normal form \(\bar{r}\cdot\hat{n}=p\):
\(\bar{r}\cdot\dfrac{1}{13}\left(3\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+12\hat{k}\right)=\dfrac{78}{13}=6\)
(i) The length of the perpendicular from the origin is \(p=6\) units.
(ii) The unit normal is \(\hat{n}=\dfrac{3}{13}\hat{i}+\dfrac{4}{13}\hat{j}+\dfrac{12}{13}\hat{k}\), so the direction cosines of the normal are
\(\left(\dfrac{3}{13},\ \dfrac{4}{13},\ \dfrac{12}{13}\right)\).

The plane passes through the point with position vector \(\bar{a}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and is perpendicular to \(\bar{n}=4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\), so \(\bar{n}\) is the normal.
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\):
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(1)(4)+(1)(5)+(1)(6)=15\)
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(4\hat{i}+5\hat{j}+6\hat{k}\right)=15\)
This is the required vector equation of the plane.

The plane passes through \(A(-1,2,3)\) and its normal has direction ratios \((0,2,5)\).
The Cartesian equation of a plane through \((x_1,y_1,z_1)\) with normal \((a,b,c)\) is
\(a(x-x_1)+b(y-y_1)+c(z-z_1)=0\)
\(0(x+1)+2(y-2)+5(z-3)=0\)
\(2y-4+5z-15=0\)
\(\therefore 2y+5z=19\)
This is the required Cartesian equation of the plane.

The required plane is parallel to the XY-plane, so its normal is along the Z-axis: \(\bar{n}=\hat{k}\), i.e. direction ratios \((0,0,1)\).
It passes through \(A(7,8,6)\). The Cartesian equation is
\(0(x-7)+0(y-8)+1(z-6)=0\)
\(\therefore z=6\)
This is the required Cartesian equation of the plane (a plane parallel to the XY-plane at \(z=6\)).

Let \(O\) be the origin and \(M(1,0,0)\) the foot of the perpendicular from \(O\) to the plane.
Then \(\overline{OM}\) is normal to the plane:
\(\bar{n}=\overline{OM}=\hat{i}+0\hat{j}+0\hat{k}=\hat{i}\)
The plane passes through \(M\) with position vector \(\bar{a}=\hat{i}\).
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(1)(1)+(0)(0)+(0)(0)=1\)
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\) is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\hat{i}=1\)
This is the required vector equation of the plane.

The plane is parallel to \(\bar{b}=4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\), so the normal is \(\bar{n}=\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\).
\(\bar{n}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\ 4&-1&3\\ 1&1&1\end{vmatrix}\)
\(=\hat{i}((-1)(1)-(3)(1))-\hat{j}((4)(1)-(3)(1))+\hat{k}((4)(1)-(-1)(1))\)
\(=\hat{i}(-1-3)-\hat{j}(4-3)+\hat{k}(4+1)=-4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\)
The plane passes through \(A(-2,7,5)\), so \(\bar{a}=-2\hat{i}+7\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\).
\(\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(-2)(-4)+(7)(-1)+(5)(5)=8-7+25=26\)
The vector equation \(\bar{r}\cdot\bar{n}=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}\) is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(-4\hat{i}-\hat{j}+5\hat{k}\right)=26\).

The plane is \(\bar{r}=(5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-3\hat{k})+\lambda(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k})+\mu(\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k})\).
It passes through \(P(5,-2,-3)\) and is parallel to \(\bar{b}=\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\) and \(\bar{c}=\hat{i}-2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}\).
Normal \(\bar{n}=\bar{b}\times\bar{c}\):
\(\bar{n}=\begin{vmatrix}\hat{i}&\hat{j}&\hat{k}\\ 1&1&1\\ 1&-2&3\end{vmatrix}\)
\(=\hat{i}(1\cdot3-1\cdot(-2))-\hat{j}(1\cdot3-1\cdot1)+\hat{k}(1\cdot(-2)-1\cdot1)\)
\(=\hat{i}(3+2)-\hat{j}(3-1)+\hat{k}(-2-1)=5\hat{i}-2\hat{j}-3\hat{k}\)
Using \(P(5,-2,-3)\), \(d=\bar{a}\cdot\bar{n}=(5)(5)+(-2)(-2)+(-3)(-3)=25+4+9=38\).
Cartesian equation \(5x-2y-3z=38\):
\(\therefore 5x-2y-3z=38\).

The plane makes intercepts \(a=1,\ b=1,\ c=1\) on the coordinate axes.
The intercept form is
\(\dfrac{x}{a}+\dfrac{y}{b}+\dfrac{z}{c}=1\)
\(\dfrac{x}{1}+\dfrac{y}{1}+\dfrac{z}{1}=1\Rightarrow x+y+z=1\)
Writing \(\bar{r}=x\hat{i}+y\hat{j}+z\hat{k}\), the vector equation is
\(\therefore \bar{r}\cdot\left(\hat{i}+\hat{j}+\hat{k}\right)=1\).
